title: Natural unrotation of a strict cone square
statement: Let g:K to L and g':K' to L' be cochain maps in an abelian category with a derived category, and let s:K to K', r:L to L' satisfy g r = s g'. Let e and e' identify their localized cone triangles with the double rotations of triangles T and T'. Set t=inr(g)[-1], t'=inr(g')[-1], alpha=r[-1], beta=Cone(s,r)[-1]. For every witness hc of t beta = alpha t', there are isomorphisms d:Qtriangle(t) to T and d':Qtriangle(t') to T' such that (Q(alpha) d'_1)[1] = d_1[1] e_2^{-1} Q(r) e'_2 and Q(Cone(alpha,beta)) d'_3 = d_3 e_1^{-1} Q(s) e'_1.

proof.text: The mappingCone.rotateHomotopyEquiv and its commutation homotopies identify the rotation of Qtriangle(g) with Qtriangle(inr(g)). Combine its inverse with mappingCone.shiftTriangleIso and Q.mapTriangleCommShiftIso at -1 to compare Qtriangle(inr(g)[-1]) with the shifted rotation of Qtriangle(g).

Compose the shifted rotation of e with rotateRotateRotateIso and shiftFunctorCompIsoId to construct d, and similarly d'. Compute its first component from shift comparisons. Compute its third component as the cone-shift inverse followed by the shifted inverse double-cone equivalence and shift cancellation, followed by e_1.

Prove degreewise that mappingCone.shiftIso.inv is natural for strict cone maps and that rotateHomotopyEquiv.inv is natural for the square (r,Cone(s,r)). Apply Q and the shift functor, then use commShiftIso naturality and shift cancellation. This proves the third-component identity; the first-component identity follows directly from the shift coherence identities.

lean.statement:
theorem derived_cone_square_unrotation
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C]
    {K L K' L' : CochainComplex C ℤ}
    (g : K ⟶ L) (g' : K' ⟶ L') (s : K ⟶ K') (r : L ⟶ L')
    (hs : g ≫ r = s ≫ g')
    (T T' : Triangle (DerivedCategory C))
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.mapTriangle.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone.triangle g) ≅
      T.rotate.rotate)
    (e' : DerivedCategory.Q.mapTriangle.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone.triangle g') ≅
      T'.rotate.rotate) :
    let t := (CochainComplex.mappingCone.inr g)⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧'
    let t' := (CochainComplex.mappingCone.inr g')⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧'
    let α := r⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧'
    let β := (CochainComplex.mappingCone.map g g' s r hs)⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧'
    ∀ (hc : t ≫ β = α ≫ t'),
    ∃ (d : DerivedCategory.Q.mapTriangle.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone.triangle t) ≅ T)
      (d' : DerivedCategory.Q.mapTriangle.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone.triangle t') ≅ T'),
      (DerivedCategory.Q.map α ≫ d'.hom.hom₁)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' =
        d.hom.hom₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' ≫ e.inv.hom₂ ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map r ≫ e'.hom.hom₂ ∧
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainComplex.mappingCone.map t t' α β hc) ≫ d'.hom.hom₃ =
        d.hom.hom₃ ≫ e.inv.hom₁ ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map s ≫ e'.hom.hom₁
